# INSIDE — Notes for Physica

## Camera discipline

- The camera is ruthless. It always tells you exactly where to look.
- There is **no HUD**. The world IS the UI. The frame does the work.
- The camera never shakes. It is steady, theatrical, secure.

## Silhouette readability

- The protagonist reads at any distance, against any background.
- The silhouette is articulated: head, shoulders, torso, hips, legs all
  distinguishable.
- Lighting sculpts the silhouette from behind (rim) and from the side
  (key), not from the front.

## Animation economy

- Every pose is animated. Even idle has subtle micro-breathing.
- The protagonist never stops being alive.
- Anticipation, follow-through, weight. Animation principles are obeyed
  even when no one is watching.

## Visual hierarchy

- Foreground (player + key props) is the brightest, highest-contrast part
  of the frame.
- Midground is darker, quieter.
- Background is nearly monochrome, atmospheric.
- The eye is led by contrast, not by HUD arrows.

## Material restraint

- Muted, slightly desaturated palette. Industrial greys, dirty whites,
  sickly yellows.
- The world feels lived-in, hostile and quiet.

## What we steal

- **No HUD policy.** Physica's prompts and dialogue live at the bottom of
  the frame, minimal, soft.
- **Silhouette readability.** The avatar and INSTRUMENTO must always be
  readable in any scene, against any background.
- **Animation economy.** The avatar should breathe. The INSTRUMENTO should
  drift. Nothing should ever be frozen dead.
- **Visual hierarchy by contrast.** The foreground puzzle reads, the
  background recedes.

## What we reject

- INSIDE's horror tone. Physica is wondrous.
- INSIDE's desaturated, oppressive palette. Physica has color, but used
  sparingly and with intention.

## Applied to Physica

- The avatar's silhouette must read against the cascade (Escena 2),
  against the gorge walls (Escena 5), against the metropolis (Escena 8).
  Rim lighting + key lighting from the side, never flat.
- The INSTRUMENTO must always float in a way that reads. Not stuck to the
  avatar, but near it, with intentional spacing.
- Animation: the avatar's walk cycle, jump, and idle must obey the 12
  animation principles (squash/stretch, anticipation, follow-through,
  arcs, etc.).
